questions.question: A clock shows the correct time at 6 AM. The clock gains 2 seconds every 5 minutes. What time (in PM) will it show at 4 PM the same day?
questions.solution:
The time duration from **6 AM** to **4 PM** on the same day is calculated as follows:

From 6 AM to 12 Noon = 6 hours

From 12 Noon to 4 PM = 4 hours

Total time elapsed = 6 + 4 = **10 hours**

The clock gains **2 seconds** every **5 minutes**.

Gain in 1 minute = 2/5 seconds

Gain in 60 minutes (1 hour) = (2/5) × 60 = **24 seconds**

Total gain in 10 hours = 10 × 24 = **240 seconds**

To convert the total gain from seconds into minutes:

Total gain = 240 ÷ 60 = **4 minutes**

Time shown by the clock = 4:00 PM + 4 minutes = **4:04 PM**

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question: Father's age 15 years ago from present was 6 times of the age of his son 3 years ago from present. Son's age after 11 years from present is 16 years. What is the ratio of present ages of father and son?
questions.solution:
Given that the **Son's age** after 11 years from the present is 16 years.

Son's present age (S) + 11 = 16

**S = 16 − 11 = 5 years**

The problem states that the **Father's age 15 years ago** was 6 times the **Son's age 3 years ago**.

F − 15 = 6 × (S − 3)

Substitute the value of S = 5 into the equation:

F − 15 = 6 × (5 − 3)

F − 15 = 6 × 2

F − 15 = 12

**F = 12 + 15 = 27 years**

Ratio of the present ages of the **Father and Son** = 27 : 5

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 3**”.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a way in which underground water reaches the surface?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Through evaporation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Springs** are natural points of discharge where the **Water Table** intersects the ground surface, allowing **Groundwater** to flow out freely due to gravity or hydrostatic pressure. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Wells** are man-made structures created by digging or drilling into the **Saturated Zone** of the earth to access and extract water for various purposes. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Tube wells** are specialized deep-bore systems that use a long pipe to reach deep **Aquifers**, employing mechanical pumps to lift water to the surface level. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Evaporation** is the physical process by which water changes from a liquid to a gaseous state and moves into the **Atmosphere**, representing a loss of water from the surface rather than a delivery method from underground. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrological Context**:

 
 
• **Aquifers**: These are underground layers of **Permeable Rock** or sediment (like sand and gravel) that contain and transmit **Groundwater**.
 
• **Infiltration**: The downward movement of water from the surface into the soil, which is the primary method of **Aquifer Recharge**.
 
• **Water Table**: The upper limit of the portion of the ground that is completely saturated with water; it can fluctuate based on **Precipitation** and extraction.
 
• **Capillary Action**: The movement of water through tiny spaces in the soil, which can bring moisture up to plant roots but is not a method for discharging large volumes of water.
 
• **Transpiration**: Part of the **Water Cycle** where plants absorb water from the soil and release it into the air as vapor.

questions.question: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form that originated in which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is a classical dance form that originated in the Indian state of **Kerala** and is recognized as one of the eight primary Indian classical dances by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**.
 
• The term is derived from the words **Mohini**, referring to the mythical enchantress avatar of **Lord Vishnu**, and **Aattam**, which means movement or dance in **Malayalam**; thus, it literally translates to the **dance of the enchantress**.
 
• It is traditionally a **solo dance** performed by women, characterized by its graceful, swaying body movements and subtle facial expressions that follow the **Lasya** style (delicate and feminine).
 
• The dance is known for its circular movements and the **Atavakul** (basic steps), which avoid abrupt jerks, mimicking the gentle flow of the backwaters and the swaying of palm trees in **Kerala**.
 
• The repertoire of Mohiniyattam includes items like **Cholkettu**, **Jatiswaram**, **Varnam**, **Padam**, and **Tillana**, primarily set to **Sopana Sangeetham** music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Classical Dances and States:**

 
 
• **Tamil Nadu:** This state is the home of **Bharatanatyam**, a dance form renowned for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and sophisticated sign language based on **hand gestures (mudras)**.
 
• **Andhra Pradesh:** It is the origin of **Kuchipudi**, a dance-drama that involves both singing and dancing, traditionally performed by men but now dominated by female practitioners.
 
• **Kerala (Other forms):** Besides Mohiniyattam, Kerala is also famous for **Kathakali**, a highly stylized classical dance-drama known for its heavy make-up and elaborate costumes.
 
 
 
• **Key Elements of Mohiniyattam:**
 
 
• **Costume:** Dancers typically wear a white or off-white **Kasavu saree** with a bright **gold-toned brocade** border, symbolizing purity.
 
• **Music:** The lyrics are usually in **Manipravalam**, a literary mixture of **Sanskrit** and **Malayalam**.
 
• **Notable Exponents:** Legends such as **Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma**, **Sunanda Nair**, and **Jayaprabha Menon** have significantly contributed to its revival and global popularity.

questions.question: During Ramadan, Muslims fast from:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dawn to Sunset**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ramadan** is the ninth month of the **Islamic lunar calendar** and is observed by Muslims worldwide as a month of **fasting**, prayer, and reflection.
 
• The act of fasting, known as **Sawm**, is one of the **Five Pillars of Islam**, which are the foundational acts of worship for believers.
 
• The duration of the daily fast begins at **Dawn** (the time of the **Fajr** prayer) and concludes at **Sunset** (the time of the **Maghrib** prayer).
 
• During these hours, individuals abstain from consuming food, drinking any liquids, smoking, and engaging in sexual relations to cultivate **self-discipline** and spiritual growth.
 
• The start and end of the fast are determined by the **local lunar sightings**, which is why the dates of **Ramadan** shift approximately 10 to 11 days earlier each year in the Gregorian calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Suhoor**:

 
 
• This is the **pre-dawn meal** eaten before the first light of day appears and the fast begins.
 
• It is a vital part of the daily routine to maintain physical strength and is considered a **blessed practice** in Islamic tradition.
 
 
 
• **Iftar**:
 
 
• This is the meal used to **break the fast** immediately after the sun sets.
 
• Following the tradition of Prophet Muhammad, many Muslims break their fast with **dates** and water before performing the evening prayer.
 
 
 
• **Laylat al-Qadr**:
 
 
• Known as the **Night of Power**, it is believed to be the night when the **Quran** was first revealed to the Prophet.
 
• It occurs during the **last ten days** of **Ramadan** and is considered the holiest night of the year.
 
 
 
• **Eid al-Fitr**:
 
 
• This major **Islamic festival** marks the end of the month of **Ramadan** and the beginning of the next month, **Shawwal**.

• The **Tiriyo**, a traditional **bamboo flute** with seven holes, is considered the most prestigious melodic instrument in Santhal music, often associated with shepherd life and romantic folklore.
 
• Rhythmic accompaniment is provided by a variety of **drums**, most notably the **Tumdak** (a two-headed earthen drum) and the **Tamak** (a large kettle drum made of metal or wood).

questions.question: Oxygen is replenished in the atmosphere mainly by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Photosynthesis**__.

__
 
• **Photosynthesis** is the fundamental biological process by which **green plants**, **algae**, and **cyanobacteria** produce their own food using **sunlight**.
 
• During this process, plants absorb **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)** and water (H₂O) from the environment and convert them into **glucose**.
 
• **Oxygen (O₂)** is released as a vital by-product into the atmosphere during the **photolysis of water** in the **thylakoid membranes** of **chloroplasts**.
 
• The overall chemical reaction can be summarized as: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
 
• This process is essential for maintaining the **Oxygen-Carbon Dioxide balance** in the Earth's **biosphere**, effectively replenishing the oxygen consumed by other life forms.

• It is a metabolic process where living organisms consume **Oxygen** to break down **nutrients** and produce **ATP** (energy).
 
• This process results in the release of **CO₂**, thereby decreasing atmospheric oxygen levels.
 
 
 
• **Combustion**:
 
 
• A chemical reaction involving a fuel and an **oxidant** (oxygen) that produces heat and light.
 
• It **depletes oxygen** from the atmosphere and increases the concentration of **greenhouse gases**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Activities**:
 
 
• Large-scale operations and the burning of **fossil fuels** in factories consume massive quantities of **Oxygen**.
 
• These activities contribute to **air pollution** and **Global Warming** by disrupting the natural gas cycles.

questions.question: Which region in India is prone to earthquakes and landslides?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himalayan region**__.

__
 
• The **Himalayan region** is geologically the most unstable and active part of India due to the ongoing **tectonic collision** between the **Indian Plate** and the **Eurasian Plate**. This convergence results in the accumulation of immense stress, which is released through frequent and high-magnitude **earthquakes**.
 
• According to the **Seismic Zoning Map** developed by the **Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)**, the entire Himalayan belt falls under **Zone V** (Very High Damage Risk Zone) and **Zone IV** (High Damage Risk Zone).
 
• The region consists of **young fold mountains** characterized by steep slopes, high relief, and fragile, unconsolidated sedimentary and metamorphic rocks. These physical features make the terrain highly susceptible to **gravity-induced mass movements** such as **landslides**, **rockfalls**, and **debris flows**.
 
• Heavy **monsoon rainfall**, sudden **cloudbursts**, and the melting of glaciers act as triggering factors, lubricating the loose soil and rock layers, which leads to frequent disasters in states like **Uttarakhand**, **Himachal Pradesh**, and **Arunachal Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• Composed of deep **alluvial deposits**, it lies between the Himalayas and the plateau.
 
• While it experiences ground shaking from Himalayan seismic events, its flat topography makes the risk of **landslides** negligible.
 
 
 
• **Peninsular Plateau**:
 
 
• Recognized as one of the oldest and most stable landmasses (**Craton**) on Earth.
 
• It has lower seismic activity compared to the north, although major exceptions like the **1993 Latur earthquake** and **1967 Koyna earthquake** indicate internal faulting.
 
 
 
• **Coastal Plains**:
 
 
• These regions are primarily vulnerable to **hydro-meteorological disasters** such as **cyclones**, **storm surges**, and **tsunamis** (notably the 2004 event).
 
• The lack of significant elevation gradients prevents large-scale **landslide** activity.

questions.question: Why was the Zabt system under Mughal Empire not implemented in provinces like Gujarat and Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inability to survey the land**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Zabt System**, also known as the **Bandobast System**, was a sophisticated land revenue assessment method introduced during the reign of **Mughal Emperor Akbar** around **1580-1582**.
 
• This system was primarily designed and implemented by Akbar's finance minister, **Raja Todar Mal**, and it relied heavily on the **Dahshala** principle, which averaged crop yields and prices over the previous **ten years**.
 
• A fundamental requirement for the **Zabt system** was the **measurement of land** and the maintenance of detailed **statistical records** regarding cultivation and productivity for each **Bigha** of land.
 
• In provinces like **Gujarat** and **Bengal**, the **Mughal administration** could not implement this system because they lacked the necessary administrative reach and historical data to perform accurate **land surveys**.
 
• The **geographic complexities** of the **Bengal delta** and the late integration of **Gujarat** into the central administrative fold made the **physical measurement** of every field logistically impossible at that time.
 
• Consequently, in these frontier or outlying provinces, the state reverted to older or less rigorous methods of revenue collection, such as **Nasaq** or **Kankut**, which did not require detailed annual **surveys**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Poor soil quality**: This was not the reason for the exclusion; **Bengal** was one of the most fertile provinces of the **Mughal Empire**, known for its high **agricultural productivity** and **monsoon-fed** crops.
 
• **Frequent foreign invasions**: While the **Mughals** faced various regional challenges, the implementation of **Zabt** was hindered more by **internal administrative logistics** and **geography** than by external military threats.
 
• **Lack of local administration**: While **Bengal** and **Gujarat** had strong local **Zamindari** systems, the specific failure was the **technical inability** to conduct **Paimash** (measurement), which was the core pillar of the **Zabt** revenue model.
 
• **Raja Todar Mal**: Apart from the **Zabt system**, he is credited with introducing standardized units of measurement like the **Gaz-i-Ilahi** and classifying land into four categories: **Polaj**, **Parauti**, **Chachar**, and **Banjar**.

questions.question: In tennis, when a player reduces the speed of his shot to land the ball just above the net and onto the opposite side, it is called a _____.

• A **Drop shot** is a delicate **touch shot** in tennis played with the intention of making the ball land just over the net, as close to the net as possible on the opponent's side.
 
• The shot is executed by reducing the speed of the racquet at the moment of impact, often using a **Continental grip** to provide better control and feel.
 
• The primary mechanical feature of a drop shot is the application of **backspin** or **underspin**, which causes the ball to lose its forward momentum and 'die' or bounce vertically upon hitting the court surface.
 
• Tactically, it is used to exploit an opponent who is positioned deep behind the **baseline**, forcing them to move rapidly forward to reach the ball before it bounces twice.
 
• Elite players like **Roger Federer** and **Novak Djokovic** are known for using the drop shot as a **deception tool**, disguising the motion to look like a standard heavy groundstroke until the last millisecond.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• A powerful **overhead stroke** hit with a motion similar to a serve, usually in response to a high **lob**.
 
• It is designed to be a **point-winning shot** by directing the ball downward at high velocity into the opponent's court.
 
 
 
• **Slice**:
 
 
• A technique where the racquet strings brush underneath the ball to create **underspin**.
 
• While the drop shot is a type of slice, a standard **slice groundstroke** travels deep into the court and stays low to the ground after the bounce, making it difficult for opponents to generate power.
 
 
 
• **Two-hand**:
 
 
• This refers to the **two-handed backhand**, a popular stroke where the player uses both hands on the racquet handle.
 
• It provides increased **stability** and **leverage**, allowing players to handle high-velocity balls and **topspin** more effectively than a one-handed backhand.

questions.question: (frac{sqrt{0.04}}{0.4}) times ((0.8)/(sqrt{0.16)}) times ((1.2)/(sqrt{0.36)}) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly calculate the **square roots**: √0.04 = 0.2, √0.16 = 0.4, and √0.36 = 0.6.

Substitute these into the expression: (0.2 ÷ 0.4) × (0.8 ÷ 0.4) × (1.2 ÷ 0.6).

This simplifies to: 0.5 × 2 × 2 = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (√0.04 / 0.4) × (0.8 / √0.16) × (1.2 / √0.36)

**Step 1:** Simplify the **square root** terms in the numerator and denominator.

⇒ √0.04 = √(4 / 100) = 2 / 10 = 0.2

⇒ √0.16 = √(16 / 100) = 4 / 10 = 0.4

⇒ √0.36 = √(36 / 100) = 6 / 10 = 0.6

**Step 2:** Replace the simplified values back into the **expression**.

⇒ (0.2 / 0.4) × (0.8 / 0.4) × (1.2 / 0.6)

**Step 3:** Perform the **division** for each fraction.

⇒ (1 / 2) × 2 × 2

⇒ 0.5 × 2 × 2

**Step 4:** Multiply the remaining values to find the **final result**.

⇒ 1 × 2 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Roots of Decimals

When finding the **square root** of a decimal, the number of decimal places in the result is always **half** of those in the original number (e.g., √0.0001 = 0.01).

BODMAS Rule

questions.question: The sum of the three consecutive even numbers is 72. What is the largest of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an **odd number** of terms in an **Arithmetic Progression**, the **average** is the middle term.

**Average** = Total Sum ÷ Count ⇒ 72 ÷ 3 = 24.

The numbers are **consecutive even numbers**, so the set is: (24 − 2), 24, (24 + 2).

The numbers are 22, 24, and 26.

The **largest number** is 26.

**∴ The correct answer is 26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of three **consecutive even numbers** = 72.

**Formula Used:** If the first even number is x, then the next numbers are (x + 2) and (x + 4).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/def1d427a81fd58898a7025288b4a0b5c448c8c8be5be4e27208f3b615e26ffe.png] 

⇒ x + (x + 2) + (x + 4) = 72

⇒ 3x + 6 = 72

⇒ 3x = 72 − 6

⇒ 3x = 66

⇒ x = 66 ÷ 3

⇒ **First number (x)** = 22

⇒ **Largest number (x + 4)** = 22 + 4 = 26

**∴ The correct answer is 26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Even/Odd Numbers

The difference between any two **consecutive even** or **consecutive odd** numbers is always 2. For consecutive integers, the difference is 1.

Middle Term Shortcut

For an **Arithmetic Progression** with n terms (where n is odd), the **middle term** is always equal to (Total Sum ÷ n).

Sum of AP Formula

The sum of an AP is given by Sₙ = (n ÷ 2) × [2a + (n − 1)d], where **a** is the first term and **d** is the common difference.

questions.question: frac{(sqrt{11}+sqrt{4})² + (sqrt{11}-sqrt{4})²}{10sqrt{15}} = ?

Apply the **Algebraic Identity**: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)

Here, a = √11 and b = √4. Numerator = 2(11 + 4) = 30.

Expression = 30 ÷ 10√15 = 3 / √15.

On **Rationalizing**: (3 × √15) / 15 = √15 / 5.

**∴ The correct answer is √15 / 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ((√11 + √4)² + (√11 − √4)²) ÷ 10√15

**Formula Used:** (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)

⇒ **Numerator** = (√11 + √4)² + (√11 − √4)²

⇒ Numerator = 2((√11)² + (√4)²)

⇒ Numerator = 2(11 + 4) = 2 × 15 = 30

⇒ **Expression** = 30 / 10√15

⇒ Expression = 3 / √15

⇒ Multiply numerator and denominator by √15 (**Rationalization**):

⇒ (3 × √15) / (√15 × √15) = 3√15 / 15

⇒ Result = √15 / 5

**∴ The correct answer is √15 / 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity (a + b)² − (a − b)²

The difference of squares of sum and difference is 4ab: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Rationalization of Denominator

To remove a radical from the denominator, multiply the fraction by the **conjugate** or the radical itself to make the denominator a rational number.

Surds Property

For any positive number x, (√x)² = x. Also, √a × √b = √(a × b).

questions.question: What is the unit digit of 242 × 367 × 847?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **unit digit** of a product, simply multiply the **unit digits** of the individual numbers.

Unit digits are 2, 7, and 7.

Calculation: 2 × 7 × 7 = 14 × 7 = 98.

The last digit is 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The numbers are 242, 367, and 847.

To find the **unit digit** of 242 × 367 × 847:

⇒ **Unit digit** of 242 = 2

⇒ **Unit digit** of 367 = 7

⇒ **Unit digit** of 847 = 7

⇒ **Unit digit** of the entire product = (2 × 7 × 7) mod 10

⇒ 2 × 7 = 14 (unit digit is 4)

⇒ 4 × 7 = 28

⇒ The **unit digit** of 28 is 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Digit of Power

The **unit digit** of a number raised to a power can be found using the **cyclicity** of the last digit. For example, the cyclicity of 2, 3, 7, and 8 is 4.

Cyclicity of 0, 1, 5, 6

Numbers ending in 0, 1, 5, or 6 will always have the **same unit digit** (0, 1, 5, and 6 respectively) regardless of the power nk (where k > 0).

Cyclicity of 4 and 9

The digit 4 has a **cyclicity of 2** (4¹=4, 4²=6) and 9 also has a cyclicity of 2 (9¹=9, 9²=1).

questions.question: The length of a rectangle is 12 cm. The diagonal of the rectangle is 13 cm. What is the area (in square cm) of the rectangle?

By using the **Pythagoras Triplet** (5, 12, 13), where 13 is the diagonal and 12 is the length.

The **breadth** of the rectangle is 5 cm.

**Area** of the rectangle = Length × Breadth = 12 × 5 = 60 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Length = 12 cm, Diagonal = 13 cm

**Formula Used:** **Diagonal² = Length² + Breadth²** and **Area = Length × Breadth**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/123cc0bb62f73cfc0bd4257f855f3d96b7d8755dec731b55ee581956a5bc57f6.png] 

⇒ (13)² = (12)² + (Breadth)²

⇒ 169 = 144 + (Breadth)²

⇒ (Breadth)² = 169 − 144 = 25

⇒ **Breadth** = √25 = 5 cm

⇒ **Area** of rectangle = 12 cm × 5 cm = 60 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagoras Triplets

A set of three integers a, b, c satisfying a² + b² = c². Commonly used triplets in exams are (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

Rectangle Formulas

**Perimeter** = 2 × (Length + Breadth) | **Diagonal** = √(Length² + Breadth²). In a rectangle, diagonals are equal and bisect each other.

Square of a Sum and Difference

The difference between the square of a sum and the square of a difference is given by **(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab**.

Sum of Squares Identity

Another useful form is **(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)**, which simplifies calculations involving addition of squared binomials.

BODMAS Rule

questions.question: Sum of the ages of two persons E and F is 50 years. The average age of E, F and G is 40 years. What is the age (in years) of G?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of ages of **E, F, and G** = Average × Total persons

Total sum = 40 × 3 = 120 years.

Sum of ages of **E and F** = 50 years.

Age of **G** = Total sum − Sum of (E + F) = 120 − 50 = 70 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 70 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of ages of **E** and **F** = 50 years.

Average age of **E**, **F**, and **G** = 40 years.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d303d3fa394027e42aadc2f1aeeaa259685d1165e9c3fd0965e329ac6ac2cf62.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of ages of (E + F + G) = 40 × 3

⇒ E + F + G = 120

⇒ We know, E + F = 50

⇒ 50 + G = 120

⇒ G = 120 − 50

⇒ G = 70 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 70 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).

Sum of N Natural Numbers

The sum of the first **n** natural numbers is given by [n(n + 1)] ÷ 2.

Weighted Average

When groups have different sizes, the combined average is (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question: X = 40 percent of 60 and Y = 50 percent of 40. What is the sum of X and Y?

**Given:**

**X** = **40 percent** of **60**

**Y** = **50 percent** of **40**

Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Total

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2da40f59dcf3a4fd1153aba1222cd918969a4e957facc56e53a96f3a1e5362d.png] 

⇒ **X** = (40 ÷ 100) × 60

Fractional Conversions

Expressing percentages as fractions simplifies calculation. For example, **50%** = 1/2 and **40%** = 2/5.

Commutative Property

In percentage calculations, a% of b is equal to b% of a. Thus, **40% of 60** is the same as **60% of 40**.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change = [(New Value − Original Value) ÷ Original Value] × 100.

questions.question: An article is sold for a loss Rs. 98. Loss percentage is 28 percent. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss percentage of 28% corresponds to a **Loss** of Rs. 98.

Unitary method: 1% of the **Cost Price (CP)** = 98 ÷ 28 = 3.5.

Selling Price (SP) percentage = 100% − 28% = 72%.

Selling Price = 72 × 3.5 = 252.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 252.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loss = Rs. 98

Loss percentage = 28%

**Formula Used:**

Loss = (Loss% × Cost Price) ÷ 100

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) − Loss

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71c4feef8114c4245de9d2e663d5e8d393244ceeff394d0aec182b6773a960af.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 28% of CP = 98

⇒ CP = (98 × 100) ÷ 28

⇒ CP = 3.5 × 100 = Rs. 350

⇒ SP = CP − Loss

⇒ SP = 350 − 98 = Rs. 252

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 252.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit or loss is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**. Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Selling Price Formula

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 when there is a profit, and SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100 when there is a loss.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is a reduction offered on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.

questions.question: The profit earned on selling an article for Rs. 1200 is 9 times of the loss incurred on selling the same article for Rs. 1000. What will be the selling price of the article to earn a profit of 20 percent?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference between the two **Selling Prices** = 1200 − 1000 = 200.

Ratio of **Profit** to **Loss** is given as 9 : 1.

Total units = 9 + 1 = 10 units ⇒ 10 units = 200.

Therefore, 1 unit (Loss) = 20. **Cost Price (CP)** = 1000 + 20 = 1020.

Selling Price for **20% Profit** = 1020 × 1.2 = 1224.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1224.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price 1 (SP₁) = ₹1200 (at Profit)

Selling Price 2 (SP₂) = ₹1000 (at Loss)

Profit = 9 × Loss

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Loss = CP − SP

New SP = CP × (100 + Profit %)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/75a0b271c85d4c973d4a4edf5a5ac9c369319eab21451074b592d5b7d5e864eb.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **Cost Price** of the article be CP.

⇒ Profit = 1200 − CP

⇒ Loss = CP − 1000

According to the question:

⇒ (1200 − CP) = 9 × (CP − 1000)

⇒ 1200 − CP = 9CP − 9000

⇒ 1200 + 9000 = 9CP + CP

⇒ 10200 = 10CP

⇒ CP = 1020

To earn a **20% profit**:

⇒ Required SP = 1020 × (120/100)

⇒ Required SP = 102 × 12 = 1224

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1224.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss/CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise.

Selling Price Formula

When profit % is given: SP = CP × (100 + P%)/100. When loss % is given: SP = CP × (100 − L%)/100.

Relation between SP, CP and MP

**Marked Price (MP)** − **Discount** = **Selling Price (SP)**. CP × (100 + Profit %) = MP × (100 − Discount %).

questions.question: Two trains are running in opposite direction with the same speed. Length of each train is 165 metres. They cross each other in 15 seconds. What is the speed (in m/s) of each train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **opposite direction**, Relative Speed = (Sum of Lengths) ÷ Time

Since **speeds are equal**, 2 × Speed = (165 + 165) ÷ 15

2 × Speed = 330 ÷ 15

2 × Speed = 22 m/s

Speed = 11 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 11 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 165 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 165 m

Time taken to cross each other (T) = 15 sec

Let the **speed of each train** be 'v' m/s.

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = Speed₁ + Speed₂

Relative Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28a8f6993478107f19f69ab3ed046e82c49e1d374e49898d96b23300894598ac.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = 165 + 165 = 330 m

⇒ Relative Speed = v + v = 2v m/s

⇒ Relative Speed = Total Distance ÷ Time

⇒ 2v = 330 ÷ 15

⇒ 2v = 22

⇒ v = 22 ÷ 2

⇒ v = 11 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 11 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: |v₁ − v₂|.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Rule

When a train crosses another train (stationary or moving), the total distance covered is always the **sum of the lengths** of both trains.

questions.question: A bus starts moving with the initial speed of 20 km/hr. Its speed increases by 10 km/hr after every hour. How much time (in hours) will it take to cover a distance of 270 km?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The distance covered in each hour forms an **Arithmetic Progression** (AP): 20, 30, 40, ...

Check the sum for 6 hours by adding consecutive terms:

20 + 30 + 40 + 50 + 60 + 70 = 270 km

Since the sum of distances over 6 hours equals the **total distance**, the time required is 6 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Initial Speed** (a) = 20 km/hr

**Speed Increase** (d) = 10 km/hr every hour

**Total Distance** (Sₙ) = 270 km

**Formula Used:**

Sum of n terms of an AP: Sₙ = (n ÷ 2) × [2a + (n − 1)d]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/98ddb6f20036902c09d125f467dd64afaedba90b11142e996c0b325daf4e70fb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 270 = (n ÷ 2) × [2 × 20 + (n − 1) × 10]

⇒ 270 = (n ÷ 2) × [40 + 10n − 10]

⇒ 270 = (n ÷ 2) × [30 + 10n]

⇒ 270 = 15n + 5n²

⇒ 5n² + 15n − 270 = 0

⇒ n² + 3n − 54 = 0

⇒ n² + 9n − 6n − 54 = 0

⇒ n(n + 9) − 6(n + 9) = 0

⇒ (n − 6)(n + 9) = 0

⇒ n = 6 or n = −9

⇒ Since time cannot be negative, n = 6 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression Sum

The sum of the first n terms of an AP is given by Sₙ = (n/2)[2a + (n−1)d] or Sₙ = (n/2)[a + l], where l is the last term.

Average Speed in AP

When speeds are in AP over equal intervals of time, the **Average Speed** is the arithmetic mean of the initial and final speeds: (a + l)/2.

General Term of AP

The nth term (speed at the start of the nth hour) is calculated as aₙ = a + (n − 1)d.

questions.question: A person sells 20 articles at Rs. 60 per article after giving 15 percent discount. He earns a profit of 30 percent. If no discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct ratio relation: **CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)**.

**CP / MP** = (100 − 15) / (100 + 30) = 85 / 130 = 17 / 26.

If no discount is given, the **Marked Price** becomes the **Selling Price**.

**New Profit** = 26 − 17 = 9 units.

**Profit %** = (9 / 17) × 100 = 52.94%.

**∴ The correct answer is 52.94 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Selling Price (SP)** of one article = ₹60

**Discount** = 15%

**Profit** = 30%

**Formula Used:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = SP / (1 − Discount%)

**Cost Price (CP)** = SP / (1 + Profit%)

**Profit %** = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a1f967e218a1ac61fd131684b7e2bb2f1008547f54f3221ea763d701f8d47346.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **MP** = 60 / 0.85 = 6000 / 85 = 1200 / 17

⇒ **CP** = 60 / 1.3 = 600 / 13

⇒ If no **Discount** is given, New **SP** = **MP** = 1200 / 17

⇒ New **Profit** = (1200 / 17) − (600 / 13)

⇒ New **Profit %** = [((1200 / 17) − (600 / 13)) / (600 / 13)] × 100

⇒ New **Profit %** = [((1200 / 17) / (600 / 13)) − 1] × 100

⇒ New **Profit %** = [(2 × 13 / 17) − 1] × 100

⇒ New **Profit %** = [26 / 17 − 1] × 100 = (9 / 17) × 100

⇒ New **Profit %** = 52.9411...% ≈ 52.94%

**∴ The correct answer is 52.94 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CP and MP Relation

The ratio of **Cost Price** to **Marked Price** is always given by CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%).

Marked Price (List Price)

It is the price displayed on the product. **Discount** is always calculated on the **Marked Price**.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁ and d₂ are given, the **Effective Discount** is d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂ / 100).

‘पुलिस द्वारा जनता को दी गई चेतावनी सूचना’ वाक्यांश के लिए सार्थक शब्द है - **__अलर्ट__**।

**

__Key Points__

**

 
• ‘पुलिस द्वारा जनता को दी गई चेतावनी सूचना’ वाक्यांश के लिए सही शब्द **‘अलर्ट’** है।
 
• **‘अलर्ट’** का अर्थ है — किसी विशेष खतरे, आपातकालीन स्थिति या महत्वपूर्ण घटना के प्रति पहले से सचेत या सावधान कर देना।
 
• जब किसी लंबे वाक्यांश या विचार को केवल एक सार्थक शब्द में व्यक्त किया जाता है, तो उसे **‘वाक्यांश के लिए एक शब्द’** कहा जाता है।
 
• इसका प्रयोग भाषा को अधिक **स्पष्ट**, **सटीक** और **प्रभावशाली** बनाने के लिए किया जाता है।
